ProjectInfo.name: VIBE / vibestart
ProjectInfo.annotation: Define the VIBE framework and the optional vibestart bootstrap/runtime product as a coherent, agent-agnostic engineering system.

Principles.principle-1: Understand the actual engineering intent behind a request instead of merely obeying the literal wording.
Principles.principle-2: Use project state, prior decisions, active work, drift signals, and verification posture as first-class context.
Principles.principle-3: Adjust workflow depth and path to the scale, maturity, and risk of the current task.
Principles.principle-4: Resist false clarity and force clarification when the shape of the work is still too ambiguous.
Principles.principle-5: Define the expected behavior and boundaries before implementation work begins.
Principles.principle-6: Treat tests, traces, review, and evidence as the basis for trust, not fluent output.
Principles.principle-7: Keep code, docs, and operational artifacts navigable through stable identifiers and structure.
Principles.principle-8: Escalate review and sync according to risk signals rather than static ritual.
Principles.principle-9: Allow autonomous work only when actions, decisions, and status transitions remain explainable and inspectable.
Principles.principle-10: Repeat key knowledge across artifacts only when the repeated view serves a different role and helps detect drift.
Principles.principle-11: Treat configuration as a readable operating contract with comments, recommended defaults, and safe review semantics.
Principles.principle-12: Require routing, projection, review escalation, and sync semantics to be explicit, reproducible, and reviewable across runtimes.

UC-001.title: Define a standalone methodology for intent-driven engineering
UC-001.precondition: Agentic development needs a stable engineering model that does not depend on one shell or one model vendor.

flow.step-1: Capture product and engineering intent in the canonical knowledge graph.
flow.step-2: Project clarified intent into requirements, execution, and verification surfaces.
flow.step-3: Run engineering work through explicit macro contracts instead of ad hoc prompting.

UC-001.postcondition: A project can adopt VIBE as a methodology without requiring vibestart.

UC-002.title: Bootstrap VIBE quickly in a real repository
UC-002.actor: Developer new to agentic workflow or team lead standardizing a project
UC-002.precondition: A repository needs a low-friction path to canonical artifacts, defaults, and operating rules.

flow.step-1: Select an explicit vibestart profile: core or deep.
flow.step-2: Install the canonical docs surface, manifest, and policy files.
flow.step-3: Apply profile-specific product behavior without changing the VIBE methodology semantics.
flow.step-4: Explain the installed surfaces, active defaults, optional extensions, and next-step contract during onboarding.

UC-002.postcondition: The repository has a usable VIBE operating surface with bounded setup complexity.

UC-003.title: Route ordinary engineering requests through a stable macro language
UC-003.actor: Agent user interacting in plain language
UC-003.precondition: The user may not want to remember or manually chain workflow phases.

flow.step-1: Treat ordinary engineering requests as implicit entries into the top-level vibe macro.
flow.step-2: Choose or recommend discover, refine, deliver, fix, sync, resume, or deploy through deterministic routing guards and explicit precedence rules.
flow.step-3: Use guided or auto execution while keeping the same macro contract.

UC-003.postcondition: The user works against one public language instead of manually juggling phases.

UC-004.title: Reduce drift through graph-first knowledge and synchronized projections
UC-004.precondition: Code, planning artifacts, and verification surfaces can diverge during autonomous work.

flow.step-1: Keep the knowledge graph as the primary knowledge spine.
flow.step-2: Project clarified intent into requirements and refined work into plan and verification artifacts through deterministic, idempotent projection rules.
flow.step-3: Run sync as an ordered reconcile-then-cleanup flow across graph, requirements, plan, verification, code, and VIBE-owned operational state.

UC-004.postcondition: Cross-validated artifacts expose drift instead of hiding it.

UC-005.title: Let advanced users tune governance without silently changing the framework
UC-005.precondition: Policy thresholds need calibration as the system is exercised on real projects.

flow.step-1: Record policy knobs in commented TOML files.
flow.step-2: Analyze runtime and review traces with the hidden calibrate macro.
flow.step-3: Suggest or apply explicit TOML diffs instead of mutating policy invisibly, and treat apply as an experimental path until deterministic guards are proven.

UC-005.postcondition: Governance evolves through inspectable configuration changes.

UC-006.title: Present a deterministic first-run contract for vibestart
UC-006.actor: Repository operator on first install or profile switch
UC-006.precondition: vibestart is invoked with --core, --deep, or no explicit profile flag.

flow.step-1: Resolve profile choice explicitly through a flag or an interactive prompt.
flow.step-2: State what is installed, what defaults are activated, and what remains optional.
flow.step-3: State the immediate next-step contract, including how plain requests will be routed and how recommendations can be confirmed.

UC-006.postcondition: The operator understands the installed product surface without guessing hidden defaults.

technical.constraint-1: knowledge-graph.xml is the primary knowledge spine and source of orchestration continuity.
technical.constraint-2: No mandatory docs/specs side-bridge is allowed; canonical knowledge must stay inside docs/*.xml and their projections.
technical.constraint-3: Projection, routing, review selection, and sync behavior must be deterministic enough that two compliant runtimes choose the same control path from the same observable state.

business.constraint-1: vibestart remains optional; VIBE must still deliver baseline engineering hygiene when its canonical files are fed directly to an agent.
business.constraint-2: Bootstrap profile choice must be explicit and must not assume that general development seniority equals maturity in agentic development.
business.constraint-3: guided and single are the normative starting defaults until auto, multi, and policy mutation paths are protected by formal guards and verification.

regulatory.constraint-1: Configuration and policy files must be self-explanatory and safe to review in version control without storing runtime secrets.
regulatory.constraint-2: Canonical contract markup and structural labels must remain in English for cross-runtime and cross-agent interoperability; localized interaction aliases are allowed only as explicit UX tokens and never as structural labels.

Glossary.term: Verified Intent-Based Engineering, an agent-agnostic methodology for intent-driven engineering.
Optional bootstrap and runtime product that installs and operates VIBE in a concrete agent environment.
The role of docs/knowledge-graph.xml as the primary semantic center of the project.
Stable public VIBE workflow contract such as discover, refine, deliver, or sync.
Lower-level implementation operator used internally to realize a macro contract.
The deterministic rules that project graph state into requirements, development, and verification artifacts.
The deterministic precedence and guard system that maps an incoming request to a VIBE macro path.
A permitted but non-normative execution path such as auto, multi, or calibrate apply, pending stronger guards and verification.
The deterministic onboarding statement that tells the operator what vibestart installed, what defaults are active, and what happens next.
The lighter vibestart bootstrap profile with a low-friction operating layer.
The heavier vibestart bootstrap profile intended for richer integrations and longer-lived projects.
